title: Social Anxiety & Fear of Judgement
description: Explore entering a room while feeling watched through dialogue, evidence and psychological reasoning.

lessons.title: What happens when you watch yourself?
lessons.teach: Follow the conversation one message at a time. Notice what the behaviour might be achieving before you decide why it happened. About five minutes.
lessons.objective: Distinguish observable evidence from a tentative explanation of entering a room while feeling watched.

nodes.title: Watch the conversation
nodes.prompt: Read the exchange one message at a time, then work from what the characters actually said.

nodes.title: What might be happening?
nodes.body:
Social-anxiety models describe how fear of evaluation can increase self-focused attention. Private sensations may be mistaken for evidence of how others see us. Safety behaviours such as rehearsing each sentence can make it harder to hear invitations to participate.

Some groups really are hostile. The question is whether the feared judgement is supported by the particular interaction.
